categories.main_business_segments: Roivant is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company with a diversified pipeline concentrated in inflammation and immunology. The company operates through multiple subsidiary companies (Vants) including Dermavant (commercializing VTAMA for psoriasis and atopic dermatitis), Immunovant (developing anti-FcRn antibodies for autoimmune diseases), Priovant (developing brepocitinib for dermatomyositis and uveitis), Kinevant (developing namilumab for sarcoidosis), and Genevant (nucleic acid delivery technology platform). Beyond therapeutics, Roivant also incubates discovery-stage companies and health technology startups.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Roivant's core technologies include topical formulations (VTAMA using aryl hydrocarbon receptor targeting), monoclonal antibodies targeting the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), small molecule inhibitors of TYK2 and JAK1, and nucleic acid delivery platforms including lipid nanoparticle (LNP) and ligand conjugate technologies. The company employs computational tools for drug discovery, development and commercialization, and utilizes a Vant model structure that enables rapid decision-making and specialized development strategies for each product candidate.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Roivant's primary markets are patients with inflammatory and immunological diseases including psoriasis (approximately 8 million U.S. patients), atopic dermatitis (approximately 26 million U.S. patients), myasthenia gravis, thyroid eye disease, chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy, Graves' disease, dermatomyositis, non-infectious uveitis, and sarcoidosis. The company serves healthcare providers, physicians, and third-party payors who make clinical and reimbursement decisions for patient access to approved products.
categories.geographic_coverage: Roivant operates globally with primary focus on the United States, European Union, United Kingdom, Canada, Mexico, Switzerland, Middle East, North Africa, and Latin America. The company is incorporated in Bermuda with principal executive offices in London, United Kingdom. VTAMA has been approved in the U.S. for psoriasis and has filed for approval in atopic dermatitis, with international expansion through partnerships such as Japan Tobacco for commercialization in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: Roivant operates at the midstream to downstream positions in the pharmaceutical supply chain. The company in-licenses drug candidates and technologies from upstream sources (such as GSK, HanAll Biopharma, and Pfizer), develops them through clinical trials, and commercializes approved products directly to patients through healthcare providers and third-party payors. Manufacturing is outsourced to third parties including GSK Trading, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Samsung Biologics.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Roivant's strategic focus is on accelerating development and commercialization of medicines in inflammation and immunology through its Vant model structure. Key R&D priorities include expanding the anti-FcRn franchise (IMVT-1402 and batoclimab) across multiple autoimmune indications, advancing brepocitinib in dermatomyositis and uveitis, developing namilumab for sarcoidosis, and leveraging proprietary computational and delivery technologies. The company plans to in-license multiple potentially category-leading drugs annually and initiate 4-5 potentially registrational studies with IMVT-1402 by March 31, 2025.
categories.revenue_model: Roivant generates revenue primarily through product sales (VTAMA generated $75.1 million in fiscal year 2024), milestone payments from in-licensing agreements, royalties on product sales, and upfront payments from collaboration partners. The company also receives revenue from technology partnerships and licensing arrangements, such as Genevant's collaboration-based business model with pharmaceutical partners. Future revenue will depend on successful commercialization of VTAMA in additional indications and regulatory approval of pipeline candidates.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Roivant competes in the biopharmaceutical industry against larger pharmaceutical companies and specialized biotechnology firms. For VTAMA in psoriasis, competitors include topical corticosteroids, roflumilast, and calcineurin inhibitors. For anti-FcRn therapies, competitors include complement C5 inhibitors (eculizumab, ravulizumab), efgartigimod, and rozanolixizumab. For brepocitinib, competitors include approved JAK inhibitors and other immunosuppressive therapies. Roivant positions itself as uniquely capable of developing transformative medicines faster through its Vant model, proprietary technologies, and capital allocation efficiency.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of May 28, 2024, Roivant had 738.7 million common shares outstanding with a market capitalization of approximately $8.0 billion as of September 29, 2023. The company received approximately $5.2 billion in net cash proceeds from the sale of Telavant to Roche and completed a $648 million share repurchase of Sumitomo Pharma's stake. VTAMA generated $75.1 million in net product revenue for fiscal year 2024, representing significant growth from launch. The company is a large accelerated filer with a robust balance sheet to fund multiple development programs.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Roivant's value proposition centers on its Vant model structure that enables rapid, entrepreneurial development of medicines with specialized management teams economically incentivized around specific products. VTAMA offers a steroid-free, once-daily topical option for psoriasis and atopic dermatitis with evidence of remittive effect. The anti-FcRn franchise (IMVT-1402 and batoclimab) demonstrates deep IgG reductions with minimal impact on albumin and LDL cholesterol. Brepocitinib offers dual TYK2/JAK1 inhibition with potentially superior efficacy in autoimmune diseases. The company differentiates through computational tools, centralized capital allocation, diversified pipeline across risk profiles, and creative deal structures that align incentives with partners.
